_role: RUNTIME manifest shape. Copy this to .autopilot/state/<FEATURE_ID>/manifest.json at register time. It is NOT the schema of the tracked authored contract under docs/autopilot-manifests/<task-slug>.json — that file is a different artifact with a different lifetime and carries NO manifest_schema_version. autopilot-review-readiness.mjs fail-closes with HALT CONTRACT_INVALID unless the manifest it is handed sits at exactly .autopilot/state/<FEATURE_ID>/manifest.json, so adding manifest_schema_version to a tracked contract does not upgrade it — it breaks register. A repo whose tracked manifests lack that string is not on an older workflow; do not open a task to migrate them. See level3-workflow.md section 11.
negative_scope: no adjacent subsystem or undeclared file
_verification_rule: Every command in `verification` must assert a PROPERTY, never a pinned literal. A literal is false the moment anything moves, and because this manifest is hash-locked after `register`, a stale literal cannot be corrected in place — it forces a full close-and-re-register cycle. EVERY ENTRY IS EXECUTED, NOT READ. runVerificationGroup() spawns each string as a shell command and gates on its exit status. An English sentence is not a command: it fails on the first attempt, every attempt. This rule used to say 'command' and then illustrate it with prose sentences, and the examples taught louder than the wording — an author copied their shape and the gate rejected all of them at register time (Plexco, 2026-07-30). So: WRITE an executable assertion of a property. "osv-scanner --format json ... | jq -e '.results | length == 0'" / "test $(jq -r '.version' <pkg-meta>) = $(npm view <pkg> version)" / "git diff --quiet <base> -- <file>" (identity to base IS the property here) / "grep -qF 'case 2b' path/to/test.ts". DO NOT WRITE prose: "osv-scanner reports zero findings" / "the diff contains no new migration". DO NOT WRITE a literal: "<pkg> == 1.2.3" / "test count == 561" / "migration tail == 0024". A 'no new migration' rule is no longer enforceable by declaring `scope` narrowly (kit v34: the diff is certified as whatever it actually is, not checked against declared scope) — assert it as an executable command instead: "git diff --name-only --no-renames \"$AUTOPILOT_DIFF_BASE_SHA\"...HEAD | grep -qE '^(migrations|db/migrate)/' && exit 1 || exit 0" (AUTOPILOT_DIFF_BASE_SHA is exported into every verification command's environment for exactly this kind of check). Observed cost: a slice that pinned `postcss == 8.5.18` in `verification.focused` needed a third registration when the owner narrowed its scope (Plexco, 2026-07-30); a sibling manifest that pinned a test-count baseline went stale within hours of being authored and HALTed its slice at MAX_ROUNDS.
_scope_rule: `scope` must list EXACT worktree-relative file paths — not directories, no duplicates. The gate rejects a directory entry. Include every file the slice will touch, including this manifest's own authored counterpart under docs/autopilot-manifests/ if the slice amends its contract.
